dedupe_keys.name: network rail open data feeds including bplan train planning data

description: Network Rail has offered a set of operational data feeds to the public since December 2012 to encourage products useful to passengers and the rail industry. Among its published datasets is BPLAN, the train planning data set, which holds network locations and sectional running times used in timetable planning and is listed on data.gov.uk under the Open Government Licence. The feeds are free, but users must create an account, access is first come, first served and limited to 1,000 users, and use is governed by Network Rail's terms and conditions, which forbid using Network Rail branding or calling an application official. Technical documentation on the formats and how the feeds work is kept by the community Open Rail Data wiki. Coverage is national for Great Britain's rail network. Caveats: Network Rail gives no guarantee of availability or uptime, and the Open Rail Data wiki could not be read on 2026-09-26, so the feed list and formats are not detailed here. The location and running-time data support rail network flow and capacity planning models, and operational feeds support resilience analysis of delays and disruptions. They are related to railML for timetable exchange.
